question:
Jordan has a list of unique projected car prices for the next several years. He needs to purchase the car in one year and sell it in another at a lower price. Jordan's goal is to keep the financial loss as small as possible.

Example:
price = [20, 15, 8, 2, 12]
His minimum loss is incurred by purchasing in year 2 at price[1] = 15 and reselling in year 5 at price[4] = 12. Return 15 - 12 = 3.

Function Description: Complete the smartCarTrade function.
Parameters: int prices[n] — a list of car prices for consecutive years.
Returns: int — the minimum loss Jordan can make.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 2 * 10^5
1 <= price[i] <= 10^16
All prices are distinct. A valid answer exists.

Sample Input 0:
3
5 10 3
Sample Output 0:
2

Sample Input 1:
5
20 7 8 2 5
Sample Output 1:
2
answer:
FUNCTION GBFS_PATH(adj, names, tone, start_idx, exit_idx):
    CREATE priority queue PQ
    CREATE list PARENT of size N, initialized to -1
    CREATE empty set VISITED

    PUSH (tone[start_idx], names[start_idx], start_idx) into PQ

    WHILE PQ is not empty:
        POP (curr_tone, curr_name, u) from PQ
        IF u is in VISITED:
            CONTINUE
        ADD u to VISITED

        IF u == exit_idx:
            CREATE empty list PATH
            WHILE u != -1:
                APPEND names[u] to PATH
                u = PARENT[u]
            REVERSE PATH
            RETURN PATH

        FOR each neighbor v in adj[u]:
            IF v not in VISITED:
                PARENT[v] = u
                PUSH (tone[v], names[v], v) into PQ

    RETURN NULL  // No path found

criteria.name: Core Algorithm Logic
criteria.description: Core Algorithm Logic (4 marks). Student applies the correct method: pair each price with its original year index; sort prices in descending order (or ascending with correct neighbor logic); compare adjacent sorted values to compute valid losses only when the purchase year < selling year; track the minimum valid loss. 4 marks: fully correct sorting-based logic with year check. 3 marks: mostly correct; minor logical inconsistency or missing detail. 2 marks: sorting present but incorrect handling of year ordering or neighbor computation. 1 mark: attempt made but solution fundamentally flawed. 0 marks: no relevant logic.

criteria.name: Efficiency and Constraints Handling
criteria.description: Efficiency & Constraints Handling (2 marks). Proposed design respects constraints: O(n log n) sorting plus O(n) scan. No nested double loops leading to O(n^2) for large n. Recognizes that price values may be large integers (up to 10^16). 2 marks: efficient and scalable. 1 mark: minor inefficiencies but workable. 0 marks: inefficient solution (e.g., checking every pair).

criteria.name: Edge Case Consideration
criteria.description: Edge Case Consideration (2 marks). Shows awareness of special/edge scenarios: already-minimal loss appearing early or late in array; closest price difference not valid if the selling year precedes the buying year (must skip); n >= 2 is guaranteed but the check is at least implied. 1 mark: edge cases logically handled. 0 marks: no edge case consideration. (Treat as binary at the 1-mark threshold; award 2 only when multiple edge cases are explicitly handled.)

criteria.name: Clarity, Structure and Output
criteria.description: Clarity, Structure & Correct Output Representation (2 marks). Pseudocode is structured, readable, and returns the right output as an integer. Variables named meaningfully (e.g., minLoss, sortedPrices); steps follow a logical order; final return/print is clear. 2 marks: clear and correct. 1 mark: understandable but messy or unclear return. 0 marks: confusing or missing output.
